mechanism.owner_quote: Expand-and-contract is a staged change protocol
mechanism.reason: Flyway covers ordered migrations, not tolerant dual representation.

invariant.owner_quote: Each phase has a compatibility gate.
invariant.reason: Flyway has no compatibility gate or dual-shape reader/writer rule.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: a migration with no contract date becomes a permanent dual schema
failure_recovery.reason: Flyway has no contract-date or forward-repair recovery.

alternative.owner_quote: A smaller change may keep the schema and add a mapping layer instead of moving authority.
alternative.reason: Flyway alternatives are migration types, not a mapping layer.

sections: GitHub's online schema migration for MySQL

mechanism.owner_quote: If backfill takes hours, it may read records while new writes occur. A design needs an authoritative writer and a change-capture/reconciliation plan.
mechanism.reason: Explains copy-while-live-writes and the change-capture/reconciliation arrangement.

invariant.owner_quote: Two independent writers are not automatically atomic just because the schema includes both fields.
invariant.reason: gh-ost README has no two-writer atomicity or dual-schema rule.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: A crash can leave a checkpoint behind the last committed row; a changed mapping can strand a subset.
failure_recovery.reason: README has no crash checkpoint or row-reconciliation procedure.

alternative.owner_quote: A stop-the-world migration or a dual-write with reconciliation may be preferable when the write rate is low or the changed-row set is small.
alternative.reason: README names modes/tools, not stop-the-world or dual-write alternatives.

entries.unit: Continuous Archiving and PITR — PostgreSQL documentation
sections: 25.3.4. Making a Base Backup Using the Low Level API
25.3.5. Recovering Using a Continuous Archive Backup

mechanism.owner_quote: A base backup plus a continuous archive of write-ahead records lets an operator restore the data to a chosen point in time before an incident.
mechanism.reason: Defines a base backup plus archived WAL restored to a chosen point in time.

invariant.owner_quote: The backup chain must be complete and restorable, and a recovery target must be validated against the application's consistency requirements, not only produced.
invariant.reason: Requires a complete restorable chain and an application-consistency check for the target.

failure_recovery.owner_quote: A missing or corrupt archive segment makes the target unreachable; run restore drills on a schedule and verify checksums and recovery completion.
failure_recovery.reason: Names missing or corrupt archive segments and requires scheduled restore drills and checksums.

alternative.owner_quote: Promote a replica for availability, but it does not protect against replicated deletion or corruption; use backups when recovery point and retained history matter.
alternative.reason: Contrasts replica promotion, which does not protect against replicated deletion or corruption.
